task.title: [P1] Profile JVM context division/precision gaps and address uncovered causes
task.body:
The user asked whether work was underway to investigate significant performance gaps against the JDK. Baseline 527 contains real gaps, but tasks 529/532/537/539 set separate optimization directions without measured attribution for the worst context division/precision rows.

Source: benchmarks/BASELINE.md and benchmarks/results/2026-10-16-macos-arm64/{summary.csv,environment.txt,binding-verified.txt,evidence.sha256}; source baseline a809e79be2085b4b8886ccbc846337af0cf918d2, integration 33f5550894eb747b791c122c854b881a363119df. BellSoft Liberica 25.0.4+9-LTS, Apple M4 Max/macOS ARM64, 3 JVM forks × 5 samples after 5 warmups. Medians of 15 batch means; these are not 15 independent processes. Other applications and swap were present, and short batches limit the stability of conclusions.

Priority observations (Krogu/JDK):
- decimal/small/divide: 970.38/31.50 ns/op, 6344.97/248.00 B/op, 30.8× the time.
- decimal/wide/divide: 1291.27/101.93 ns/op, 8253.97/352.00 B/op, 12.67×.
- decimal/negative-scale/divide: 704.10/42.75 ns/op, 4393.99/316.00 B/op.
- decimal/large-scale/divide: 695.15/44.39 ns/op, 4393.99/316.00 B/op.
- decimal/wide/precision: 89.52/3.72 ns/op, 728.00/16.00 B/op, 24.1×.
Exact expressions and 16 prepared input slots: benchmarks/src/commonMain/kotlin/bench/Workloads.kt and the project's generated JDK mirror. divide uses MathContext(34, HALF_EVEN); precision is measured on prepared, warmed immutable operands. These data precede integrated 533 and do not promise the current ratio.

Scope:
1. On a fresh, explicitly pinned HEAD, repeat the same priority workload IDs against the pinned public JDK, preserving the original inputs, rounding, result/cohort, warmup/forks/samples, DCE and source/artifact binding. Compare with original 527 and separate the effect of already integrated 533. Do not run heavy profiling outside the serial heavy slot.
2. Profile only the project's own Krogu code: CPU/call paths and allocation distributions by type/call site; measure profiler overhead and separate profile runs from uninstrumented paired timings. Treat causes as hypotheses until supported by evidence. Do not read OpenJDK or third-party numerical library sources/implementations; the JDK remains a public black-box comparator.
3. Provide workload→measured cause→specific fix/ticket mappings. Route compact representation to 529, multiplication to 532, parse/format to 537 and platform thresholds to 539; do not duplicate their scope. 535 is an opt-in batch API, not an automatic fix for legacy chains; 538 modular workloads are absent from the 64-case baseline.
4. Address uncovered context division/precision causes here or in a specific narrow leaf task with its own evidence and checks; do not create a generic “speed up everything” ticket. If a particular gap disappears in fresh measurements, record that instead of applying an unnecessary optimization.

Acceptance:
- A reproducible report with pinned environment/flags, exact workload IDs/input semantics, source/artifact hashes, raw samples and time+allocation profiles; quantitative attribution to the project's own paths, with sampling/GC/JIT limitations.
- Confirmed changes have independent source review and correctness oracle/invariant checks for all affected rounding modes, scale/cohort, zero/cancellation, extreme scales/range and subclass dispatch. Common numerical changes pass the necessary JVM/JS/Wasm/macOS ARM64 regression checks.
- Before/after reruns use the same expressions and inputs; time, allocation and available peak memory are shown separately, including regressions and small/wide controls. No arbitrary promise to “catch up with the JDK by a factor of N” and no timing assertions in correctness tests.
- The report explicitly distinguishes implemented/measured work, routed/pending work and remaining hypotheses; a plan or creation of a leaf task does not count as an executed speedup.
- New worktrees/logs/probes stay under project-local .codex-work/<task>/; do not change other people's active worktrees or historical evidence.

activity.text: Acceptance clarification from root: precision must first separate warm repeated observation on the existing prepared immutable operands from first-observation/cold-construction scenarios. Compare identical public construction/input/observation paths for Krogu and JDK, preserve setup exclusion and avoid mutating/clearing foreign private caches. Do not infer arithmetic regression from a cached-versus-uncached mismatch; any new cold benchmark is separately named and never substituted for the original527 precision workload. Reproduce the original warm workload unchanged, then report both scopes explicitly. Exact original JVM Krogu artifact SHA256:089a414d64ddc7822e0174227689c309603ff28772a189967303b17473dad3aa (build/libs/krogu-math-jvm-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar). Baseline numerical/harness source a809e79be2085b4b8886ccbc846337af0cf918d2; artifact and source manifests live under benchmarks/results/2026-10-16-macos-arm64, with binding-verified.txt confirming pre/post campaign equality. Correction to body path: the101-entry report/raw index is benchmarks/results/evidence.sha256, NOT inside the date directory. After integrated533 (main e95836f97e91433b49b005f9589ca6d359bfa2ac) a fresh same-workload pinned JDK/Krogu baseline is required; original ratios must not be relabelled current. No597 implementation/profile run is authorized before532 acceptance or separately agreed serialized slot. Task remains todo; this is acceptance metadata, not executed evidence.
